title: Is BIS certification mandatory?
content: BIS certification is basically voluntary. However, for products covered by a Quality Control Order (QCO), the Central Government makes conformity to the relevant Indian Standard and use of the BIS Standard Mark compulsory. BIS publishes the list of products under compulsory certification along with the governing QCOs.

title: What is the ISI Mark?
content: The ISI Mark (Standard Mark) is the certification mark granted under Scheme I. BIS grants a licence to use it after assessing the manufacturer's manufacturing and testing capability and confirming that the product conforms to the relevant Indian Standard through testing. The scheme has operated since 1955.

title: What is a Quality Control Order (QCO)?
content: A Quality Control Order is a notification by the Central Government that makes conformity to one or more Indian Standards, and use of the BIS Standard Mark under a licence or Certificate of Conformity, mandatory for a specified product. QCOs are issued on grounds such as safety, health, the environment, prevention of unfair trade practices and national security.

title: What is the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS)?
content: The Compulsory Registration Scheme (Scheme II) applies to notified electronics and IT goods. The manufacturer gets the product tested by a BIS-recognised laboratory, applies online through the CRS portal (crsbis.in), and on registration may use the BIS Registration Mark. CRS does not involve a BIS factory inspection.

title: What is the difference between the ISI Mark and CRS registration?
content: The ISI Mark (Scheme I) is a licence and involves assessment of the manufacturer's factory and testing capability. CRS registration (Scheme II) applies to notified electronics and IT goods, is based on laboratory test reports, uses the BIS Registration Mark, and does not involve a factory inspection.

title: How does a manufacturer outside India get BIS certification?
content: Manufacturers located outside India apply under the Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) to obtain a BIS licence to use the Standard Mark on products exported to India. Applications are made online through the BIS portal (manakonline.in). CRS products have an equivalent route for foreign manufacturers.

title: What is hallmarking?
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ defines hallmarking as "the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in precious metal articles." In India gold and silver are hallmarked, under IS 1417:2016 and IS 2112:2014 respectively.

title: What is HUID?
content: HUID stands for Hallmark Unique Identification. Since 1 July 2021 a hallmark consists of three marks: the BIS logo, the purity of the article, and a six-digit alphanumeric HUID number that is unique to the article. It can be checked using the BIS Care App.

title: Which gold purities can be hallmarked?
content: The BIS Hallmarking FAQ lists the permitted gold caratages for hallmarking as 14K (585), 18K (750), 20K (833), 22K (916), 23K (958) and 24K (995) fineness.

title: How much does hallmarking cost?
content: According to the BIS Hallmarking FAQ, hallmarking charges are Rs. 45 per article for gold (minimum Rs. 200 per consignment) and Rs. 35 per article for silver (minimum Rs. 150 per consignment), plus applicable taxes and levies.

title: Does a jeweller have to register with BIS?
content: The BIS jewellers page states that any manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor or retailer selling hallmarked gold or silver articles must be registered with BIS. Jewellers with an annual turnover up to Rs. 40 lakh are not mandatorily required to register, and artisans doing job work may be exempted.

title: Is there a fee for jeweller registration?
content: No. The BIS jewellers page states that the certificate of registration is granted instantly without any fee and is valid for lifetime. Application is made online through the National Single Window System portal or manakonline.in.

title: Does packaged drinking water need BIS certification?
content: Yes. BIS states that packaged drinking water (IS 14543) and packaged natural mineral water (IS 13428) are under compulsory BIS certification under the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales) Regulation, 2011, and cannot be manufactured or sold except under the BIS Certification Mark.

title: How do I check if my gold is really hallmarked?
content: According to the BIS Hallmarking FAQ, look for three marks on the article (BIS logo, purity, and a six-digit HUID) and enter the HUID in the BIS Care App to verify it. Each detachable part and each item in a pair should have its own HUID, and the jeweller must provide a 10x magnifying glass.
